title: How do we use a known product with decimals?
description: A whole number product is given, and five point nine six times twenty four point eight is found from it by writing both numbers as fractions. The digits after the point are counted to place the point. Keeko doubts that the product is fourteen point seven eight zero eight.
teaching_notes: One idea: a known product of whole numbers gives the product of decimals once the digits after the point in both numbers are counted and added. Watch for students who count the digits of the answer instead of the two numbers.

video_script.why: The child has seen that the digits after the point in a product are those of the two numbers added, and now uses a known whole number product.
video_script.substitution: the book's given product, five hundred and ninety six times two hundred and forty eight, and five point nine six times twenty four point eight
video_script.anchor: A known product of five hundred and ninety six and two hundred and forty eight, used to find five point nine six times twenty four point eight
video_script.wrong_answer: fourteen point seven eight zero eight
video_script.wrong_move: A common slip counts two digits after the point in each number, four in all, and puts the point after four places in one hundred and forty seven thousand eight hundred and eight. This gives fourteen point seven eight zero eight, far below the size check of about one hundred and fifty.

final_answer.spoken: one hundred and forty seven point eight zero eight

maths_rules: digits after the point: 5.96 has 2, 24.8 has 1, so the product has 2 + 1 = 3, and 1000 has three zeros
the slip: counting 2 and 2 gives 4 places, 14.7808, far from 150
video_script.design: One idea: the fractions have 100 and 10 at the bottom, so the given whole number product goes over 1000. Assumes the writing of a decimal as a fraction and the digit count. Wrong idea: counting two digits for each number. The given product stays all video; the decimal appears only on the answer beat.
